barriers.description: Ethical and safety constraints prevented direct testing in real emergency conditions, forcing reliance on theoretical, expert-advice, and controlled simulations.
barriers.justification: These constraints limited the team's ability to study real user behaviour under stress, conduct realistic evaluations, and thus manage evolving user understanding and evaluate designs in true contexts of use.
barriers.reference_excerpt: However, when considering the design process for a fire extinguisher, the ethical tenet of safety of research participants had to be at the forefront of the chosen methodology. Therefore, the adopted research methods listed next emphasize theoretical research, advice from professionals, and controlled environments during practical research. In conclusion, this project highlights the importance of a user-centered design process when designing equipment to be used in emergency situations, even though the ethics surrounding fire and fire studies make it difficult to do direct testing and research activities.

barriers.description: The work remained at concept stage without a functioning prototype, preventing rigorous testing, usability trials, and empirical validation of performance parameters.
barriers.justification: Lack of a physical prototype constrained the designers' ability to evaluate designs with users, iterate based on observed usability issues, and specify validated requirements (e.g., weight and activation force) for the target demographics.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The next stage in the design process would be to produce a functioning prototype, which would enable further testing and evaluation to confirm that the design is a viable improvement. As the proposed design reached only the concept stage, weight was not calculated, but the initial product evaluation conducted for the redesign indicated a total weight of 2 kg (when full).

barriers.description: Observed maintenance processes and records existed for public buildings but not for private residential dwellings, limiting empirical insight into home-maintenance behaviours.
barriers.justification: This contextual/data gap hindered the designers' ability to fully understand the private use and maintenance context of extinguishers, affecting the 'understand context of use' workload and the specification of realistic maintenance-related requirements.
barriers.reference_excerpt: The maintenance checks were thorough, and the records for extinguishers in public environments were extensive. No comparable process exists in private residential dwellings.
